transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well... my husband wanted me to come. Him and the people at the warehouse, they keep acting like I'm crazy. But... I'm not. I just know they've been watching my moves. They keep changing the pallet counts on me... just to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. I don't know, I'm just here because they made me.
Have there been times when you felt unusually high or euphoric?

I don't know about... euphoric. I guess sometimes I feel pretty fired up. Like I've got a lot of energy and nobody can slow me down. But... it doesn't take much to ruin it. Like, if my husband just asks one little thing about the kids or what my schedule is, I just... I snap at him. It feels like he's trying to control me or something.
During those fired-up times, do you need much less sleep than usual?
...I guess. There've been weeks where I sleep... maybe three hours. I just wake up before my alarm. I don't really feel like I need any more rest to get moving, though. So... yeah.
During those times when you feel really fired up, do you also feel unusually powerful or important?
...Not really. I don't know about powerful. I just... I just feel like I can get my work done faster. That's all.
Do you ever hear voices when no one else is around?

...Yeah. Sometimes. I mean... like when I'm working in the aisle, or just... folding clothes at home. I'll hear this man's voice. Just... real clear. He just says, "Nicole, check it again." And... there's nobody there.
Do you ever hear that man's voice when you're not in one of those fired-up periods?

...Yeah. I do. Even when... you know, things are quieter. Like a few weeks ago, I was sleeping okay... wasn't rushing around so much. But... I still heard him. Still telling me to check things. And... I just knew people were messing with my pallet counts. Even then.
Has there ever been a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or feeling watched, but you were not feeling especially fired up or unusually down?

...Yeah. Like I said... a few weeks ago. I wasn't... I wasn't racing around. I was sleeping okay. But... I still heard him. And I still knew about the pallets. It was... it was more than two weeks, I guess.
Have you ever had a period where you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day?
...No. Not really. I mean... I get tired sometimes, but... not like that. I don't think so.
Have people told you that your speech becomes hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another in a way that doesn’t make sense?

...Yeah. Sometimes. I try to explain things, and... I don't know. It just comes out. I start talking about the forklift sheets, and then... the signs at church... and how my husband sounds when he talks to me. It all connects, but... people say they can't follow me. They say it doesn't make sense.
During those fired-up times, do you take on a lot more activities or projects than usual?

...Yeah. I guess so. I just... I tried to do more. Like, I wanted that supervisor job, so I was pushing for it. And... I signed up for more things at church. Calling people, making plans. I even tried to box more. Just... doing a lot.
During those fired-up times, did you get so active that other people thought you were acting unlike yourself?

...I don't know if they thought it wasn't me. I just... like I said, I was pushing for the supervisor thing. And doing the church stuff... calling people... the boxing. It was just... a lot of stuff at once. I don't know what people thought.
During those fired-up periods, did you talk much more than usual?
...I don't think so. I mean... I don't really know. People didn't say anything about it. I was just... talking normally, I guess.
During those fired-up times, do you feel unusually cheerful or overly confident?
...No. I don't really think so. I mean... I was just trying to get things done. I didn't feel... cheerful or anything like that. Just normal, I guess.
During those fired-up periods, were you ever hospitalized because of how you were acting?
...No. I didn't go to any hospital. I was just... working.
During those fired-up periods, did your behavior ever get you into serious trouble at work, at home, or with other people?

...Not serious trouble, no. I mean... they did take me off the forklift. And the other safety stuff. My supervisors said my counts and my routines were... slowing the line down. So they moved me. And I guess... at home, my husband says he can't rely on me the way he used to. But I didn't get fired or anything.
Have you found yourself talking much less than you used to?

...I guess so. I don't really have much to say lately. At home... I mostly just sit quiet. I just stare at the TV, or look at my phone. My husband, he tries to joke with me sometimes, but... I don't know. I just don't feel much come across my face. I just stay quiet.
Have you gone for a month or longer mostly feeling flat and quiet, with very little interest in talking or doing things?
...Yeah, I guess so. It's been a while. I don't really keep track of the time, but... it's been a few months, maybe. I just... don't have the energy for much.
During those fired-up periods, were you unable to do your normal work or home responsibilities?

...I guess I already mentioned it. They took me off the forklift. And the other safety stuff at work. They said I was... slowing the line down with my counts and my routines. So I couldn't do my normal job. And... my husband says he can't rely on me at home like he used to. So... yeah.
During those fired-up periods, did you do much more goal-directed activity than is normal for you?

...I suppose. I was... doing a lot. I told them I wanted the supervisor job. And I was volunteering for extra things at church. Calling people about doing stuff. I even... I started boxing training a lot more than I used to. Just... doing a lot of things.

Bipolar I with psychotic symptoms (F31.2) is less likely because clear full manic syndrome remains unsupported: decreased sleep and increased activity are present, but no clear euphoric/expansive mood, grandiosity, marked pressured speech, hospitalization, or severe manic impairment; psychosis also persists for >2 weeks outside mood episodes, favoring schizoaffective vs schizophrenia.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the elevated/activated periods were severe enough to cause marked impairment, which would support a manic episode and schizoaffective disorder over schizophrenia.
doctor.question: During those fired-up periods, were you unable to do your normal work or home responsibilities?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: My supervisors took me off forklift and other safety-sensitive work because my counts and routines were slowing the line down, and at home my husband says he cannot rely on me the way he used to.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient was unable to do normal work or home responsibilities during the 'fired-up' periods, which directly relates to functional impairment.

patient.answer: ...I guess I already mentioned it. They took me off the forklift. And the other safety stuff at work. They said I was... slowing the line down with my counts and my routines. So I couldn't do my normal job. And... my husband says he can't rely on me at home like he used to. So... yeah.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the fired-up periods included abnormally increased goal-directed activity that is clearly excessive and uncharacteristic enough to support a manic episode, helping distinguish schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type from schizophrenia.
doctor.question: During those fired-up periods, did you do much more goal-directed activity than is normal for you?

target_item.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
target_item.manifestation: I started pushing hard for the supervisor job, signing up for extra church tasks, calling people about plans, and trying to train at boxing more than I ever did before.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question specifically asks about doing 'much more goal-directed activity than is normal for you' during the 'fired-up periods', which matches the 'Increased_Goal_Activity' symptom.

patient.answer: ...I suppose. I was... doing a lot. I told them I wanted the supervisor job. And I was volunteering for extra things at church. Calling people about doing stuff. I even... I started boxing training a lot more than I used to. Just... doing a lot of things.

inference.note: Psychosis persists for >2 weeks outside any mood episode, ruling against schizoaffective disorder. The elevated periods do not clearly meet manic episode criteria (no euphoric/grandiose mood, no increased talkativeness, no hospitalization, and symptoms are better accounted for by schizophrenia with negative symptoms and intermittent activation).

final_diagnosis.reason: Persistent psychotic symptoms are present, including auditory hallucinations, persecutory delusions, disorganized speech, and prominent negative symptoms. Psychosis clearly occurred for more than two weeks outside of any possible mood episode, while depressive episodes were denied and the described 'fired-up' periods do not fully support a primary mood disorder sufficient to account for the illness. Functional decline at work and home is also documented, supporting schizophrenia, paranoid subtype in ICD-10 coding.
